A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mobile-R1. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, training-stage comparisons, unseen-app evaluations, reward curves and qualitative trajectories.

after.justification: v3 reports revised original results and adds AndroidControl evaluation, physical-device experiments and a rollout-step sensitivity study.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5-VL-3B backbone, three-stage training procedure, action space, GRPO objectives and GPT-4o trajectory rewards are retained. The revised exploration-step limit is an experimental setting change, without a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on English AndroidControl Low/High settings and on physical devices, extending language and environment coverage beyond v1's Chinese benchmark experiments. AndroidControl was previously cited for annotation guidance, without reported evaluation. The Chinese dataset and 500-trajectory benchmark remain.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds evaluated GUI-R1-3B and GUI-R1-7B comparators, previously only discussed. The new AndroidControl comparison includes OS-Genesis-7B, OS-Atlas-7B, Aguvis-7B and OdysseyAgent alongside Qwen2.5-VL-7B. This substantially expands the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 introduces Low/High Type Match and Exact Match evaluation, a 50-task physical-device experiment, and comparisons at 6, 10 and 14 rollout steps. Appendix D changes the reported maximum exploration steps from 10 to 14. The collection count changes from 1,185 to 1,510 instructions, matching Table 2 in both versions. Unseen-app reporting drops task success. Figure 13 inconsistently describes its varied steps as training, inference and rollout steps.

E4.justification: v3 adds training-stage comparisons on physical devices and an analysis of tail success versus rollout length. The existing unseen-app analysis moves to Appendix E with revised accuracy results and omitted task-success results; reward and pass@k analyses are also revised. The existing qualitative cases are retained, including those moved from Appendix E to F.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained pass@k sampling procedure and GRPO rollout counts do not introduce new uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces Mobile-R1's accuracy/task-success/tail-success values of 84.42/49.40/53.60 with 78.55/30.60/37.40 and revises UI-R1 and training-stage results. GUI-R1-7B now exceeds Mobile-R1 in task success, 32.60 versus 30.60. Unseen-app accuracy changes from 84.53 to 77.78, and its task-success entries disappear. Reward and pass@k curves change; AndroidControl, physical-device and rollout-length results are added. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The GRPO objective, normalized advantage, trajectory formulation and reward equations are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs appear; the added benchmark metric descriptions concern evaluation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same method, dataset, benchmark and exploration/error-correction claims. The conclusion still claims superiority over all baselines in all metrics despite the revised evidence.

C2.justification: v3 revises the reward-convergence explanation and acknowledges accuracy decline for Mobile-R1 on unseen apps while retaining the Stage 3 generalization attribution. It adds explanations linking the English TM-Low deficit to model size, the physical-device Stage 1 dip to action-level pretraining, and longer exploration to task success. The principal mechanism explanation and limitations paragraph remain.

D1.justification: Most implementation details and prompts remain unchanged, but Appendix D revises the exploration cap to 14 steps. The resource statement changes from active open-sourcing language to explicit placeholder links and release upon acceptance, while Appendix B.2 retains the claim of 1,007 released trajectories. This establishes changed access information, not independently verified resource withdrawal.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to OS-Atlas, Aguvis and GUI Odyssey and positions Mobile-R1 against them in English-task evaluation. The related-work survey and conceptual comparison in Table 1 remain essentially unchanged. AndroidControl's additional bibliographic entry corresponds to work already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in experimental discussion, metric abbreviations, the resource statement and appendix organization. Unseen-app analysis moves to a new Appendix E, and qualitative results become Appendix F. The abstract, introduction, method exposition and most appendix prose are retained.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is substantially reorganized: Table 3 becomes a compact single-column table, an AndroidControl table is added, and unseen-app Table 4 becomes appendix Figure 12. Physical-device and rollout-length plots are added, and reward/pass@k plots are redrawn with revised axes. Existing method diagrams, dataset histogram, prompts and qualitative illustrations are retained, with several relocated.

improvement.justification: English and physical-device evaluations broaden evidence for generalization, and the rollout study adds useful analysis. However, v3 retains an all-metrics superiority claim despite GUI-R1-7B's higher task success in Table 3, and its English discussion overlooks Aguvis's higher Low-EM score, 89.4 versus 87.1. Unexplained result replacements, omitted unseen-app task-success scores and inconsistent training/inference labels further limit interpretation. These benefits and reporting problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
